title: The Zeal of the Spirit and the Trial of the Blind Man
english: Driving toward power, for the arrows of the powerful are ineffective. And do not marvel if the shepherds of Christ and teachers of piety avenge the truth; but even if one is not a teacher, not having trusted in a teaching throne, but having simply received the word of Christ and being in the rank of a disciple, he ought to have zeal for God, and to render rewards to the benefactor in speaking freely, and to speak on behalf of the truth, and to contend against impiety, so that he may hear from the Holy Scripture: 'Child, contend for the truth, and the Lord God will fight for you.'

It is nothing to marvel at if the holy ones avenge piety. Often [God] is called something through leniency, as a good God, and the prophets do not forgive piety being struck by the leniency of God. God says through Moses: 'Say to Pharaoh, Let my people go;' (Exodus 5:1) but if you do not want, behold, I will send signs, and I will strike you. Moses struck [the word] upon the word, and understanding is given to the pious, and he says: Do not think that he has a people out of equality, and God has a people. And Having contended, let not the great goodness and leniency of God hinder him, and let him not think he is opposing God, having heard: 'Your people, and My people,' the proclamation refers. Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: 'Let my people go;' (Exodus 5:1) but if you do not want, behold, I will send signs, and I will strike you and your servants; so that you may know that the earth and its fullness belong to the Lord (Psalm 24:1).

the land heard the people and the people, and did not follow the word, but says, 'All the earth is the Lord's.' For even if God used leniency, this does not betray the masterly authority. For this reason also God spoke thus, so that the zeal of the pious might be stripped bare. But the faithful also always love to exceed the words of God; for the Savior says to the disciples: 'What do men say the Son of Man is?' (Mark 4:36) One of the disciples says...

of him: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.' May the zeal of the Holy Spirit teach you also to be zealous, and to suffer for the sake of piety, and to contend the good struggle for the sake of righteousness.

For it is worthy, the imitating of good teachers, to be good disciples, as also Paul says: 'Become imitators of me, just as I also of Christ' (Matt 9:27). Do you wish to learn whether even the simple disciple, having the rank of a disciple, ought to have zeal for piety? Listen how Christ healed the one blind from birth; but rather let us hear from the beginning of the history. For after many things having been said to the evangelist, thus he began to say: 'As Jesus was passing by, he saw a man blind from birth' (John 9:1). And his disciples asked him, saying, and the following (John 9:2). And having spat, and having made clay, he anointed his eyes, and said to him: 'Go, wash in the pool of Siloam'; and having washed, he looked up (John 9:6-7). The Jews knew him, and they say: 'Is not this the one sitting for alms, being blind?' (John 9:8). Others were saying, 'Yes'; others, 'No', but 'he is like him' (John 9:9). He was saying, 'It is I' (John 9:9).

But the Pharisees and the rulers of the Jews, seeing that the wonder has many attracting to Christ, being bitten by the zeal of impiety, and being struck by the sting of the truth, call the once-blind man in. And it was to see an evil theater, of piety being avenged, and of evil judges judging, and of a great advocate contending, and of God rewarding and overseeing. They call the once-blind and having seen again, the children of the Jews, and they set him in the midst of the council, and say to him: 'Tell how you received sight, and who opened your eyes to you, and what he did to you?' (John 9:15). These things they said, not that they might know, but that by the form of the question they might instill fear. For often the form of the question becomes to the one asked a teacher to answer, or to be silent; as if someone were to say to someone...
